name: Channel 5 - Trial & Eureka (realistic close-up objects)
about: Reference: 'Why Old Soda Bottles Couldn't Stand Up', 'Why Vending Machines Used to Take Washers', 'Why Darwin's Potatoes Wouldn't Cook', 'Why a Cup Still Had Ice After a Car Fire', 'Why Your Shirt Doesn't Unravel Like a Bag of Rice'. Realistic 3D close-ups of everyday objects (glass, liquid, cork, steel caps, brass coins, magnets, glossy paint), shallow depth of field, warm studio light: a dark teal subway-tile wall over a walnut bar counter, or a mint studio backdrop with mechanism parts. 'Why X' history-of-engineering stories, 70-80 s, no characters, one calm narrator, short phrase captions in small white text.
paint_style: Photoreal 3D product close-up, warm studio light, shallow depth of field, glass and metal
formula: hook: the odd object or fact itself in close-up + 'Why...?'
the old way: how it was done and why it made sense
the problem: what kept going wrong (leaks, cheats, failures), shown on the object
the inventor's trial and error: each attempt in close-up, one per line
the eureka fix in slow detail; payoff: it is still in your hand today
